newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts look armed to capture 115-25 peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts look armed to capture 115-25 peak.

text.p: Underpinned by solid support at 115-02, September gilt futures on LIFFE will look to break above the recent contract high of 115-25 on Wednesday, analysts said.
Gilts have been consolidating since last week, filling a gap between 115-07 and 115-02 and cementing good support there.
Analysts said they could now be ready for an upside assault.

"As long as 115-02/114-30 support holds, gilts are going to be very bullish, and going to look to break above those recent highs," said David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London. He said a combination of extention and trendline targets suggested a move to 116-08, then to 116-30.
By 0705 GMT, September gilts stood 4/32 higher at 115-16.
"It had every excuse to go down so far and it's held up very well," said Sneddon, adding that a move towards 116-00 and possibly slightly above was likely in the coming sessions.
"I could see it certainly breaking out the top of the range today, but I doubt we'll see 116-30," he added.
An initial trigger for gains would be 115-18, Sneddon said.

On the downside, 114-30 is the high on July 14 and captures the top of the previous range. Further support comes in at 114-28, and more importantly at 114-25/23, which marks price action and a support line from the July and June range, Sneddon said.
Analysts at Chase in London said Tuesday's price action to a high of 115-16 confirmed 115-02 as firm support, suggesting a test of the 116-09 channel resistance on the daily chart.
"From 116-09 it might scale back, but a possible correction from here should be minor," they said in a client note.
Bullish momentum would be underlined on a break of 116-09, allowing a move to 117-25, and if above there to 121-01, the all time high traded in October 1993, Chase analysts said.
A decline below 115-02 should be confirmed by a close below 114-30, showing a move to 114-06 and 113-22, which was unlikely.
December short sterling was at 92.60 at 0726 GMT, up 0.01.
